modules.name: Project format and gamerobotics play
modules.why: Unblocks testing with real people now; every later module needs one place for a robot's settings.
tasks: One project directory: robot file, personalities, behaviours (projects/lexjr; the two robot descriptions merge in M1)
gamerobotics play: start sim body, daemon, camera, app in order; stop them together
Health checks: camera (names the app holding it), CPU throttle, missed ticks, sim not answering
Plain-word messages for each health problem, with the fix
One install (or managed environments the user never sees): gamerobotics setup
Live run with the webcam: camera check, start, monitor, Ctrl+C stop
Verify on a clean Mac: install to first wiggle under 10 minutes
Verify live: an OBS camera clash gives the right message
done_when: A clean Mac reaches LexJR looking at you in under 10 minutes, one command
An OBS camera clash produces the right message
risks: MediaPipe's numpy pin and mjpython make a single environment fiddly
notes: Built 2026-10-20 (gamerobotics f642db1, lexjr-sim c8a0fc0): play, setup, doctor, projects; three personalities.
Tested here: headless runs start, monitor and stop cleanly; a second daemon and a process dying are reported; Ctrl+C stops everything; setup builds fresh environments; 16 SDK and 46 lexjr-sim tests.

Live run with the webcam (2026-10-20): camera check 30 fps with a face in 60 of 60, all four processes ready, ~4 ms ticks, clean stop. It showed flapping slow-tick warnings from single-tick spikes; fixed with a median and a debouncer.
Not yet tested: a real OBS camera clash, and a clean machine.

modules.name: Addressable API: everything reachable by address
modules.why: The key rule: every client (CLI, dashboard, later a remote one) talks to APIs by address and never depends on running locally. Then LexJR on the Mac to a Pi walker is a new address, not a rewrite.
tasks: gamerobotd: the same JSON-RPC over a WebSocket, localhost by default, next to the unix socket
Runner control API in the app: slots and owners, switch a behaviour, live parameter changes, load or save a personality
Supervisor status API in play: processes and their state, health messages, start and stop
The CLI uses these APIs (gamerobotctl and gamerobotics), so it is the first client
Jitter histogram in the daemon's state: tick period p50, p99 and worst, over the last minute

Guardrails: API servers on their own threads; one state encode a tick shared by all subscribers; slow clients drop frames; no video, meshes or logs on the control API; the runner's control API on its own thread
Measure: tick time and jitter unchanged with the dashboard subscribed at 20–50 Hz and intents streaming at 50 Hz
Tests: every dashboard action is possible through the APIs alone
done_when: Everything play's terminal shows and the camera preview's keys do is available through the APIs
Measured: the loop's tick time and jitter (p99, worst) are the same with the API in use as without
risks: Scope creep into the parked remote access: no pairing or discovery yet, localhost only
A gateway or encoder slipping into the control thread: guarded by design and by the measurement

modules.name: Dashboard: a Tauri app over the API (Mac dev build)
modules.why: Reachy Mini's shape: a Tauri desktop app over the daemon. The second client of the API, with no back-end work of its own; it also makes hardware bring-up easier.
tasks: Tauri 2 shell (Mac, unsigned dev build): window, app icon
Connection by address: local daemon by default; the address is a setting (later: lexjr.local, walker.local)
Start and stop the project when the target is local (through the supervisor API); just connect when it is remote
Health bar and messages; process states
Robot view: 3D from the robot's model and live joint positions
Controls: torque, joint sliders, a look-at target
Behaviours: slots, switching, personality presets and live sliders, save as mine
Bring-up panel: per-joint ticks for calibration (for H0)
done_when: Everything you do with play and the camera preview today, you can do from the dashboard
Pointing it at another address needs no code change
risks: Tauri toolchain on Intel macOS: check early
Keep it a dev build: signing, installers and Windows stay parked

modules.name: Hardware bring-up: LexJR tethered
modules.why: Every later choice (the parts catalogue's numbers, packaging, whether LexJR needs a Pi) depends on how the real robot behaves. Tethered over USB to the Mac, the Reachy Mini Lite way.
tasks: FeetechIo: the RobotIo for Feetech servos over rustypot (sync read and write in ticks, one transaction a tick), tested against a fake serial port
gamerobotd --io feetech, with the servo bus port and baud in the robot file
Servo setup per joint in the robot file: ID, zero, direction, ratio
Bench bring-up with one servo: ID, 7.4 V supply, torque on and off, a move
Calibration helper: torque off, move each joint by hand, read ticks, write zeros and directions
Measure: loop tick time and jitter on the real bus, command latency, gravity sag vs the sim, a BAM check on one servo
play lexjr on the real robot (a hardware target in the project), face follow and cat gaze
Record the measurements in the spec; update the sim where it disagrees
done_when: The real LexJR follows a face through gamerobotics play, tethered to the Mac
Measured timing, latency and sag are in the spec, and the sim's assumptions are checked against them
risks: Power: servo current and the supply
Serial timing through the Waveshare board on macOS

modules.name: Parts catalogue and assembly compiler
modules.why: The keystone: every Build experience produces a robot file of kit parts, and this turns it into a running robot. Removes the LexJR hard-coding.
tasks: Catalogue format: geometry and mesh, mass and inertia, mounts, actuator model, limits, modes
First parts: STS3215 (BAM moved out of sim_bam.py), spur N:1, brackets and links, wheel, webcam, IMU, battery and board
Compiler: robot file to MJCF, daemon robot file, chain, motion config, capabilities
Derived limits and speeds; gears as generated joint equalities
Generic sim body: run any compiled MJCF, one BAM model per actuator
Regression: LexJR as parts compiles to today's limits; golden replays pass
New robot: a pan-tilt head from the catalogue runs cat gaze and mimic tilt unchanged
done_when: LexJR recompiled from parts matches today (±57° torso, 183.3°/s) and passes the golden replays
A pan-tilt head written as a file runs the behaviours unchanged
risks: Part geometry (brackets, links, mounts) is CAD work, not code

modules.name: Checker
modules.why: Gates everything a creator, or an LLM, builds; turns mistakes into plain words.
tasks: Mounts compatible
Joint range free of collisions
Static torque at a few poses within each actuator's limit
Battery and board can feed the servos
Archetype's required capabilities present
Machine-readable problems for the LLM
done_when: Every broken robot in a test set caught with the right message
LexJR and the pan-tilt head pass

modules.name: Capabilities and needs
modules.why: Behaviours target capabilities, not robots: what makes them run everywhere.
tasks: Compiler emits capabilities; robot.info reports them
Behaviours declare needs; the Runner refuses mismatches and names what's missing
MotionCore's gaze config from the gaze capability, for any chain
done_when: Cat gaze refused on a robot with no camera, with the reason
Gaze works on the pan-tilt head from its capability alone

modules.name: LLM builder (describe it)
modules.why: The most inspiring way in, and it needs no 3D UI: it drives the compiler and checker directly.
tasks: Tool interface: list_parts, start_from, add_part, connect, set_param, check, explain
Propose, check, fix loop until it passes; then show it in the sim and explain it
Archetype prompts and examples
CLI first: gamerobotics build "a robot that..."
A test set of descriptions; measure the pass rate
done_when: Most test descriptions produce robots that pass the checker and run their archetype's behaviour in sim, without hand fixes
risks: LLM reliability: mitigated by the tool-only interface and the checker

modules.name: Balancing archetype
modules.why: The first archetype beyond heads, and the first with real dynamics.
tasks: STS3215 wheel mode in the catalogue
Velocity targets through RobotIo and the body protocol
Wheel-mode actuator model (bench data needed; first guess until then)
IMU in the sim, through the body protocol
balance primitive in the daemon: classical controller first
Reference two-wheel balancer; cat gaze on its head while it balances
done_when: The reference balancer balances in sim and recovers from a push while cat gaze runs
risks: Largest sim-to-real gap; real balancing waits for hardware and a fitted wheel model

modules.name: Snap builder
modules.why: Hands-on building; the most UI work, so it waits for a stable compiler, checker and file format.
tasks: Browser 3D view of the compiled MJCF
Kit tray; snap to mounts
Derived limits, capabilities and checker messages live
Edits the same robot file as the LLM builder
done_when: A pan-tilt head and a balancer can be built by hand and run in sim

microduck adapter (JSON-RPC to robotd)

decisions.q: API first: every client (CLI, dashboard, remote) talks to APIs by address, never depending on running locally; then the Tauri dashboard as the second client, Reachy Mini's shape
Optimize for the best performance per OS, even with separate builds for Mac and Windows; the API never sits inside the control loop
Run tethered over USB first, the Reachy Mini Lite way (the laptop runs everything); platform packaging (desktop app, Windows, containers, onboard Pi, browser) parked as ideas until after bring-up
Onboard computer, when it comes: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (parked with the onboard runtime)
Balance controller: classical first, RL later through the same primitive?
Who designs the kit's brackets and links, and are they a buyable kit?
Which LLM for the builder, local or hosted?
decisions.default: any capable model through the tool interface

decisions.q: Browser stack for the studio and snap builder
Build: a kit of parts, LLM and snap builders, archetypes to start from
Our own daemon, JSON-RPC, no microduck dependency
Test 'a robot is a file' with a second robot from LexJR's hardware (pan tilt, files only)
A third robot, a two-wheeled rover: robot.approach in metres; the base's pose in the gaze chain with a diff drive in the daemon; unlimited travel
Combine the pan tilt and the rover into one robot without changing the daemon
